definitions.explanation: A festival celebrated on July 7th (or August 7th in some regions) based on the legend of two star-crossed lovers, Orihime and Hikoboshi, who can meet only once a year across the Milky Way.

examples.japanese: {七夕祭|たなばたまつ}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: To go to the Tanabata festival.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仙台|せんだい}→仙台：30730_sendai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{七夕祭|たなばたまつ}り⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧だ。
examples.english: Sendai's Tanabata festival is the most famous in Japan.

examples.english: On the night of the Tanabata festival, the children wrote their wishes on paper strips and hung them on bamboo branches.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{七夕|たなばた}→七夕：05633_tanabata⟧ (Tanabata; the seventh evening) and ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧ (festival). The festival originates from a Chinese legend about the weaver princess ⟦{織姫|おりひめ}→織姫：25130_orihime⟧ (Vega) and the cowherd ⟦{彦星|ひこぼし}→彦星：26047_hikoboshi⟧ (Altair), separated by the ⟦{天|あま}の{川|がわ}→天の川：05050_amanogawa⟧ (Milky Way) and allowed to meet only on the seventh day of the seventh month. The most iconic tradition is writing wishes on colorful paper strips (⟦{短冊|たんざく}→短冊：13674_tanzaku⟧) and hanging them on bamboo (⟦{笹|ささ}→笹：04407_sasa⟧).
